newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BIERHOFF OUT FOR EIGHT WEEKS AFTER ANKLE OPERATION.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BIERHOFF OUT FOR EIGHT WEEKS AFTER ANKLE OPERATION.

text.p: Oliver Bierhoff, who scored the two goals which won this year's European championship final for Germany, underwent surgery in a Munich clinic on Tuesday for torn ligaments in his right ankle and will be out until the end of January, surgeon Werner Keyl said.
"Bierhoff will be out for eight weeks," the surgeon said. Keyl carried out the operation on the 28-year-old striker who scored twice for his Italian club Udinese in a 3-1 win over Parma on Sunday.
"It was a relatively serious operation because he had already suffered a similar injury to the same foot a year ago," Keyl said.
Keyl said the 30-minute operation had been successful. He said Bierhoff would have to wear a plaster cast for 10 to 12 days but should be able to leave hospital within the next few days.

Bierhoff was Germany's hero in the European championship final at Wembley last June when he came on as a second-half substitute and scored both his side's goals in their 2-1 victory over the Czech Republic.
